title: A Question About The Correct Workflow.
author: Disastrous-Screen296
selftext: could one really make individual levels in separate sessions and then somehow link them together under one structure for the game? i've tried this on claude using sonnet and it linked five separate levels that were developed months and sessions apart into one game, so I wonder if this workflow could work for a bigger game with 100 levels or so. what are the concerns? how to overcome them? just what is the best addition to make this workflow practical without breaking the project as it builds up? any help would be appreciated.

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body: Can you elaborate? What do you mean by level?

replies.author: Disastrous-Screen296
replies.body: Stage. I made separate stages long before I made the base of the game (the main menu, map, score system etc) and when I asked Claude to link those levels to the game structure, it did with no problem which surprised me. However and like I said, I’m wondering if I can work with this mechanism for something if a bigger scale rather than just a game with five levels as a test.

replies.author: HealthyWest6482
replies.body:
Yeah for sure.

You probably need to write a basic schema. Shit like this is all architecture. Take your vision and articulate it in plain English (you want multiple stages tied to a menu that ties to a map and a score system, be specific) -> pass it to Claude. Say "hey Claude, this is my vision with the current project layout; can you create a markdown file that organizes this idea into structured architecture for expansion". Clarify that you want to author many stages over time and focus on hardening your foundation to allow it.

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body: You dont develop a game one level at a time. You design and implement across the whole project.

replies.author: Disastrous-Screen296
replies.body: the game’s base already calculates scores from across the levels just fine, despite each of them being created separately. But that’s the thing I’m concerned about; it’s only five levels so obviously this workflow is working on a smaller scale. What do you suggest for a larger scale project using Claude? What’s the best structure.
